transcript:
Meeting header:
Title: Crimson Bridge - Onramp & Implementation Kickoff
Recorded at: 2027-04-05 13:30 PDT
Duration: 1:02
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Nambiar (Redwood SE), Evan Cole (Crimson Bridge - Head of Platform), Marta Ruiz (CTO), Samir Patel (SRE), Lina Zhao (Product)

Summary: Quick alignment on scope for a 4-week onramp -> pilot. Primary asks: VPC/private deployment checklist, security docs (SOC2/ISO), basic bench plan for latency/cost, and sandbox credentials. Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs and initial scale targets.

Topics: onboarding timeline; network/peering/VPC; data residency & KMS; pilot success metrics; sample benchmarking; roles & approval flow.

Action items (as captured during call): see metadata.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for carving this hour for us, I'm Jordan Hayes from Redwood, I'll run through the agenda and then hand over to Priya for the technical bits. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Evan: Doing well, thanks. Loud office today but we are good.
[00:18] Marta: Hi, Marta here. Ready to get moving on this, we've got exec interest so want to make the pilot fast.
[00:25] Jordan: Great. Quick note—today's goal is to align on onramp steps, get network/security needs captured, and nail down a target date for the pilot. Priya, take us through the high-level deployment options.
[00:37] Priya: Sure. So Redwood gives three lanes — the hosted API for quick start, Dedicated reserved pools if you want predictable throughput, and Private which is the VPC/on-prem option. For Crimson Bridge since you mentioned regulated customers and internal PII, likely Private or Dedicated with VPC peering is the usual path. We usually recommend starting in Hosted for a smoke then move pilot to Dedicated or Private for perf/security testing, but we can align to whatever your security team prefers.
[01:05] Samir: Quick Q — what does Private mean network-wise? Is Redwood running anything in our VPC or do we host an appliance?
[01:15] Priya: Good question — Private has two forms: customer-managed control plane with our agents running in your VPC, or a boxed on-prem install for air-gapped. For cloud VPC mode we provide a deployment template (Terraform/CloudFormation) that creates an EKS cluster or GKE nodes, and we only need service endpoints opened for health and metrics. We also support cross-account peering. There's a checklist we'll send that shows exact ports/sgs.
[01:38] Evan: That checklist is important—our network team will want subnets and sample routes. Do you have examples for Azure as well?
[01:45] Priya: Yes — we have AWS, GCP, and Azure templates. I will attach Azure examples; I think Jordan has a consolidated packet too.
[01:53] Jordan: I'll drop the VPC checklist and sample subnet configs after this call.
[01:58] Marta: Re: keys — we need KMS/HSM integration details. We use AWS KMS and have an HSM provider for certain customers. How's key management handled?
[02:07] Priya: Redwood Private integrates with your KMS; we can use customer-managed keys. For Dedicated we offer KMS integration too but keys are in our tenant unless you bring HSM. We also log key access in audit trails. We'll share the KMS integration doc.
[02:20] Lina: On data retention — we need guarantee that telemetry and prompts are not used for model training.
[02:27] Jordan: That's standard — we offer tenant-level data controls and retention settings, plus contractual language. We'll include the explicit clause in the docs.
[02:34] Samir: Any SOC2/ISO stuff I can hand to our compliance team?
[02:38] Jordan: Yes, SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001 evidence, pen test summaries, and our architecture diagrams — I'll send the security pack.
[02:45] Marta: Great. Now on pilot metrics — what do you typically measure? Latency, cost per 1k tokens, P50/P95?
[02:55] Priya: Exactly — P50/P95 latency, throughput (requests per second), cost per 1k tokens, and error rates. Also memory/KV cache hit rates for stateful chat flows. For the pilot we'd run a set of representative prompts with sequence length distribution you provide.
[03:12] Evan: We'll share two payload profiles — short chat queries and long multimodal-ish extraction tasks. Can you run benchmarks for both?
[03:20] Priya: Yep. We'll run both on a Hosted baseline and a Dedicated/Private run to show delta. Note: quantized model variants can change latency/cost tradeoffs; we'll call those out.
[03:33] Samir: How long do benchmark runs typically take? We have a tight timeline.
[03:37] Priya: For a representative set, usually 24–48 hours to get stable stats; we can do a smoke in a few hours. For full perf matrix — 48 hours.
[03:45] Jordan: Proposed schedule: VPC/network checklist to you by 2027-04-06, sandbox creds provisioned by Crimson Bridge by 2027-04-06, initial smoke the week of 2027-04-08, full benchmark 2027-04-10–11, pilot review 2027-04-12. Sound okay?
[04:03] Marta: That timeline works if we can get security docs today.
[04:07] Jordan: We'll send the docs this afternoon.
[04:09] Lina: On roles — who will have access to the sandbox and what RBAC levels can you configure?
[04:15] Priya: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC is per-team and per-route; you can set read-only observers, ops, and admin roles. We'll show a sample role mapping.
[04:29] Evan: One more — what are fallback strategies if a model variant fails or latency spikes? We need graceful degradation.
[04:36] Priya: Redwood has routing policies and automatic fallback to compatible model variants or region failover. We can configure canary rollouts and automatic fallback to a lower-cost but higher-latency variant. Also surge capacity options for Dedicated.
[04:51] Jordan: On pricing/commits — we'll outline Hosted per-token, Dedicated reserved pools (monthly commit), and Private license fees. I'll include sample math for expected throughput and unit costs.
[05:02] Marta: Please include an example for our projected 1000 QPS peak and 10M tokens/month.
[05:09] Jordan: We'll model that.
[05:12] Samir: Are there known gotchas — infra things we should prep for?
[05:17] Priya: Watch for large KV cache sizes — that affects memory footprint. Also, if you have long-running chat contexts (>8k tokens) we'll recommend specific kernel/quantization profiles. We'll flag those in the bench doc.
[05:31] Evan: Perfect. For contacts — who's our primary from Redwood for day-to-day?
[05:36] Jordan: That's me (AE) and Priya as the SE. I'll be primary for onboarding and commercial, Priya will lead the technical run and be the bench owner.
[05:46] Marta: Ok. Any security review meeting required? Our legal wants a short call with your security lead.
[05:52] Jordan: We can set that up — I'll introduce you to Samir (Redwood security) and drop the security pack.
[05:58] Jordan: Any other questions?
[06:00] (brief hold / background noise)
[06:10] Lina: Not from Product. One ask — can we get a short runbook for failover and escalation?
[06:15] Priya: Yes, we'll provide a runbook template and an incident contact list.
[06:21] Jordan: Great. Quick recap and next steps before we close.
[06:25] Jordan: Action items — I will send VPC checklist, pricing examples, security docs; Priya will prepare benchmark plan; Crimson Bridge to provide staging access and confirm stakeholders. Proposed pilot review 2027-04-12 at 10:00 AM PT.
[06:42] Evan: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[06:45] Marta: Thanks, talk soon.
[06:47] Jordan: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with the packet.

Recap / Notes:
- Pilot window targeted for 2027-04-10 to 2027-04-12 with review on 2027-04-12 10:00 AM PT.
- Security pack and VPC checklist to be shared same day.
- Benchmarks: Hosted baseline + Dedicated/Private runs, typical 24–48h with smoke in a few hours.
- RBAC/SSO: SAML + SCIM supported; sample role mappings to be provided.

References/Links to share (mentioned on call):
- VPC checklist (will be attached)
- SOC2 and ISO evidence pack (will be attached)
- Benchmark plan template (SE to provide)

End of transcript.
